one_line: Sanskrit-educated Bengali physician who helped introduce anatomical dissection at Calcutta Medical College in the 1830s.

appearance.age_look: Early 40s, medium height, slightly lean with a bookish but quietly resilient build.
appearance.face: Oval face with a high forehead, light brown complexion, straight nose, neat trimmed moustache, alert dark eyes behind round wire-rim spectacles, default expression calm and thoughtful with a hint of resolve.
appearance.hair: Dark, neatly combed hair gathered under a plain white Bengali Brahmin-style turban (paghri) wrapped low and tight, with no ornamentation and a small knot of hair suggested beneath at the back.
appearance.costume: A long off-white cotton kurta reaching just below the knees, side-slit for ease, worn over ankle-length plain white dhoti with neat pleats at the front; over the kurta a pale beige woollen shawl with a thin maroon border draped around the shoulders like a scholarly wrap, simple brown leather slippers on the feet, and a narrow red-and-white sacred thread faintly suggested diagonally under the kurta neckline; the textiles are matte, lightly creased, and unpatterned except for the shawl border.
appearance.signature: A well-used early 19th-century anatomical atlas held in one hand, its dark brown leather cover worn at the corners, with a folded roll of parchment notes and a single slender metal dissection scalpel tucked carefully into the atlas’ strap.

ref_desc: Madhusudan Gupta is a light-brown–skinned, early-40s Bengali physician with an oval face, round spectacles, dark hair under a plain white turban, wearing an off-white kurta, white dhoti, beige shawl with maroon border, brown slippers, and carrying a worn dark-brown anatomical atlas with a tucked scalpel.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model sheet of Madhusudan Gupta: an early-40s Bengali physician with light brown skin, an oval face, high forehead, neat trimmed moustache and thoughtful dark eyes behind round wire-rim spectacles, his expression calm and quietly determined. His dark hair is hidden beneath a plain white Bengali Brahmin-style turban wrapped low and tight, with no ornamentation, suggesting a small knot of hair at the back. He wears an off-white cotton kurta that falls just below his knees with subtle side slits, over a neatly pleated ankle-length white dhoti, the fabrics matte, lightly creased, and unpatterned. Over his shoulders is a pale beige woollen shawl with a thin maroon border running along the edges, draped evenly like a scholar’s wrap, and he has simple brown leather slippers on his feet; subtly indicate a narrow red-and-white sacred thread suggested under the kurta neckline without exposing the torso. In one hand he holds a worn early 19th-century anatomical atlas with a dark brown leather cover and scuffed corners, and tucked securely under its strap is a slender metal dissection scalpel and a rolled parchment of notes. Use a restrained palette of off-white, pale beige, maroon accents, dark brown for the book and slippers, and soft black for hair and lines, presenting him front-facing in a neutral stance with clear views of face, turban, garments, and the signature atlas with scalpel.
